title: The Daily Five
dek: Five questions on today's Israeli sports headlines, from a 1968 Olympic coin-flip to a Europa League cameo in Turkey.

questions.question: Israel's 1968 Olympic quarter-final against Bulgaria in León finished 1-1. With no penalty-shootout rule yet in place, how was the winner decided?
answers: Captains drew lots from a hat
A coin toss by the referee
questions.explanation: Captains Mordechai Spiegler of Israel and Bulgaria's captain each drew a slip from a hat, and Israel's was the losing slip, sending Bulgaria through.

questions.question: Australian short-track skater Steven Bradbury pulled off one of the most unlikely gold medals in Olympic history at Salt Lake City 2002. In which event?
questions.explanation: Bradbury won gold in the men's 1,000m short-track final after leaders Ohno, Ahn, Li and Turcotte crashed out near the finish, leaving him to cross first.

questions.question: Before returning to Hapoel Galil Elyon on a long-term deal, 18-year-old guard Karem Ashkenazi spent last season with Maccabi Tel Aviv's youth academy. What was his scoring average there?
questions.explanation: With Maccabi Tel Aviv's youth team he averaged 8.1 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game, per ONE.

questions.question: Israeli international Gabi Kanichowsky came off the bench in the 61st minute of a 1-0 win away to Trabzonspor in a Europa League play-off first leg. Which club was he playing for?
questions.explanation: Kanichowsky replaced Philippe Rommens in the 61st minute for Ferencváros, who won 1-0 in Trabzon thanks to a Kristoffer Zachariassen goal.

questions.question: What punishment did UEFA hand Hapoel Tel Aviv after flares were lit by fans during the club's Conference League qualifier against Ludogorets Razgrad?
answers: A €40,000 fine plus a one-match away-ticket ban suspended for two years
A full stadium closure for one European match
A points deduction in European competition
questions.explanation: UEFA fined Hapoel Tel Aviv €40,000 and imposed a conditional, two-year-suspended ban on away ticket sales for one European match over the Ludogorets flares.
